rclpy

### 'ros2 doctor --report' output

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce issue

Run a simple node which uses an async callable object as a subscription callback:

```python
import rclpy
from std_msgs.msg import String

class AsyncCallable:
    async def __call__(self, msg):
        print(msg)

with rclpy.init():
    callback = AsyncCallable()

    node = rclpy.create_node('test')
    node.create_subscription(String, '/data', callback, 10)

    rclpy.spin(node)
```

Then publish something it should be able to react to:
```bash
ros2 topic pub /data std_msgs/msg/String '{data: "Hello"}'
```

### Expected behavior

The node should print all the published messages.

### Actual behavior

The node prints nothing and we may get a runtime warning if warnings are enabled: `RuntimeWarning: coroutine '...' was never awaited`

### Additional information

I suspect the culprit to be the coroutine check in `await_or_execute`: https://github.com/ros2/rclpy/blob/101c9f5ffbf5aa8aacbdfe7f745723f1d83694c4/rclpy/rclpy/executors.py#L202

Async callable objects do not count as coroutine functions. Passing `callback.__call__` instead in the above example would work since `inspect.iscoroutinefunction` does unwrap bound methods.

StackOverflow has a question+answer about that which even provides a possible solution: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72382098/how-to-check-if-a-callable-object-is-async-using-inspect-module-python

Or perhaps it would be better to call the function unconditionally and check if the result is awaitable:
```python
async def await_or_execute(callback: Callable[[*Ts], Awaitable[T] | T], *args: *Ts) -> T:
    """Await a callback if it is a coroutine, else execute it."""
    result = callback(*args)
    if isinstance(result, Awaitable):
        return await result
    return result
```

P.S.: I wrote this report from memory without direct access to a ROS2 environment to validate my code on. Errors are to be expected.
new_candidates.title: Async callable objects are not valid subscription callbacks

### Steps to reproduce issue

1. mkdir linorobot2_rosidl_issue
2. cd linorobot2_rosidl_issue
3. git clone https://github.com/linorobot/linorobot2_hardware.git
4. cd linorobot2_hardware/firmware
5. Edit platformio.ini and search down to the esp32 section and uncomment the board_microros_distro part of the section and set board_microros_distro = rolling
6. git checkout rolling
7. pio run -e esp32
8. Observe build failure ending in: Failed   <<< rosidl_buffer [1.13s, exited with code 2]


### Expected behavior

Builds successfully

### Actual behavior

Build failure

### Additional information

Since #1030 (09658f1, "rosidl_buffer: preserve CPU backend across RTLD_LOCAL DSO boundaries"), rosidl_buffer/include/rosidl_buffer/buffer.hpp fails to compile when RTTI is disabled. Embedded builds such as micro-ROS compile with -fno-rtti, and they build rosidl from source, so every micro-ROS Rolling build now fails at rosidl_buffer. The lyrical branch doesn't have this change and still builds.

Error (micro_ros_platformio, ESP32 target, building the rolling branch):

.../rosidl/rosidl_buffer/include/rosidl_buffer/buffer.hpp:599:29: error: cannot use 'typeid' with '-fno-rtti'
.../rosidl/rosidl_buffer/include/rosidl_buffer/buffer.hpp:599:69: error: cannot use 'typeid' with '-fno-rtti'
gmake[2]: *** [CMakeFiles/rosidl_buffer.dir/build.make:79: CMakeFiles/rosidl_buffer.dir/src/c_helpers.cpp.obj] Error 1
Failed   <<< rosidl_buffer [2.87s, exited with code 2]

Cause: #1030 added a typeid(...).name() comparison as a fallback in Buffer::as_cpu_impl(). The dynamic_cast that was there before is inside a template, so GCC only rejects it under -fno-rtti if the template is actually used. A C-only consumer like c_helpers.cpp never uses it, which is why it compiled before. The typeid expression, by contrast, is rejected as soon as the header is parsed.

Suggested fix: compile the typeid fallback only when RTTI is enabled. With RTTI off, the code then behaves exactly as it did before #1030:

cpp
template<typename A>
static CpuBufferImpl<T, A> * as_cpu_impl(BufferImplBase<T> * impl) noexcept
{
  if (!impl) {
    return nullptr;
  }
  if (auto * cpu = dynamic_cast<CpuBufferImpl<T, A> *>(impl)) {
    return cpu;
  }
#if defined(__cpp_rtti) || defined(__GXX_RTTI) || defined(_CPPRTTI)
  if (std::strcmp(typeid(*impl).name(), typeid(CpuBufferImpl<T, A>).name()) == 0) {
    return static_cast<CpuBufferImpl<T, A> *>(impl);
  }
#endif
  return nullptr;
}

The #include <typeinfo> added in the same commit could go under the same guard, though including it is harmless.

To reproduce: build any micro-ROS firmware against Rolling, e.g. with micro_ros_platformio and board_microros_distro = rolling, or compile a file that includes rosidl_buffer/buffer.hpp with g++ -fno-rtti.

Seen in: https://github.com/linorobot/linorobot2_hardware/actions/runs/45952872989
